open_obligations: Check whether inserted bugs differ in distribution from natural LLM errors.
Note the domain change from summarisation to code, where bugs are more objectively checkable.
Check whether reference bugs reduce over-trust in critiques or only make critique-bug inclusion measurable.
out.other_title: No ground truth for topic-based summarization; labelers may over-trust model summaries
out.rationale: Saunders et al. state their summarisation task has no objective way to validate answers or critiques and that labelers may misevaluate answers by trusting the model summaries too much. McAleese et al. have contractors insert subtle bugs into model-written code, asking them to verify that an LLM critic misses each bug in at least one of three samples (not strictly enforced). They note that contractors may struggle to validate the correctness of free-form critiques and to spot important issues that critiques miss, and say the tampering approach provides high-quality, difficult reference bugs which ground the ranking task by allowing contractors to more easily discriminate between critiques catching and missing the problem.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: contractor-inserted subtle bugs in model-written code, collected adversarially against an LLM critic as training data and used as reference bugs that ground the ranking of critiques, set against a topic-based summarisation task that lacks a robust or objective process for validating answers or critiques

text: The paper collects training data by having contractors introduce bugs (tampers), verifying with access to an LLM critic that it misses each bug in at least one of three samples (not strictly enforced). The authors report this adversarial collection noticeably increased bug subtlety, and the critic used was updated twice, so much data was adversarial to ChatGPT and much to an early CriticGPT.
title: Adversarial tampering: humans insert subtle bugs that an LLM critic misses
